stories.transcript: The summer I turned twelve, my parents sent me to Camp Wahkeena, up on Pine Lake. On the last night, our counselor Danny built the campfire extra high and told us about the lantern. He said an old caretaker named Mr. Abbott used to row across the lake every night with a lantern, calling for his dog, Biscuit. One stormy night the boat came back empty, and ever since, if you sat by the water after midnight, you could see his light moving across the lake. Everybody laughed. But later, my friend Maya and I snuck down to the dock, and there it was. A small yellow light, low on the water, drifting toward the far shore. We didn't say a word. In the morning there was an old leather dog collar lying on the dock, still wet. I kept it. Danny swore he had nothing to do with it, and I never found out who did.

Every Halloween we drove out to Grandpa Joe's farm in Iowa, and every Halloween he told us the same story. He said the scarecrow in the back field, the one he called Old Hollis, got cold on October nights and walked up to the porch to sit by the fire. My little brother Sam believed every word. So one year, I think it was 1996, Sam and I made a plan to stay up and catch him. We sat by the window with a flashlight and a bag of candy corn, and of course we fell asleep. In the morning, Old Hollis was sitting on the porch swing, wearing Grandpa's red wool scarf, with a mug of cocoa next to him. Grandpa swore up and down he never touched him. Grandma just smiled and refilled the mug. I still have that scarf. It still smells a little like wood smoke.
